facts: The paper 'Paying to Play: How Parliamentary Candidates Fund Ruling Party Campaigns in Malawi' was written by Michael Wahman and Merete Bech Seeberg.
The study was published in Comparative Politics on October 1, 2022 (DOI: 10.5129/001041522x16436471926538).
The paper investigates the sources of incumbent parties' superior campaign wealth in parliamentary elections in Africa's clientelistic democracies.
Prior scholarship primarily attributed ruling party wealth advantages to direct access to state resources.
Wahman and Seeberg propose that ruling parties attract candidates who are willing and able to spend their own personal resources on campaigns in hopes of securing access to central state resources.
The authors evaluate their hypothesis using original survey data collected from candidates in Malawi's 2019 parliamentary election.
Empirical findings show that government party candidates receive more funds from their party and spend significantly more of their own personal money on campaigns.
The authors conclude that candidate self-financing has important implications for political representation and competitive elections across Africa and beyond.
